sentences.text: Fossils of this animal reveal jaws that lack teeth and feature low, protruding rims without a crest.
The holotype specimen, which defines the species, is a snout fragment measuring approximately five centimeters long.
Harry Govier Seeley first referred three toothless snout fragments from the Lower Cretaceous Cambridge Greensand of England to the genus Ornithocheirus in 1869.
Seeley then provisionally named these fragments a separate genus called Ornithostoma, derived from Greek words for "bird" and "mouth".
In 1891, Seeley formally named the type species Ornithostoma sedgwicki and referred pelvis elements to it, claiming they were identical to Pteranodon.
In 1914, Reginald Walter Hooley incorrectly referred additional specimens, including a skull fragment with a crest base and postcranial fragments, to Ornithostoma.
S. Christopher Bennett considered Ornithostoma distinct from Pteranodon due to jaw ridges but concluded it was a nomen dubium in 1994.
David Unwin rejected the nomen dubium status in 2001, arguing Ornithostoma is a valid genus in Pteranodontidae with a wingspan of 2-3 meters based on limited material.
In 2012, Alexander O. Averianov suggested Ornithostoma belongs to Azhdarchoidea based on a combination of jaw and postcranial traits.
Subsequent studies suggest Ornithostoma is a member of the family Chaoyangopteridae.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Ornithostoma as Azhdarchoidea.
The species formerly known as Ornithostoma orientalis was renamed Bogolubovia orientalis and transferred to the family Azhdarchidae.
